meta.name: Soft Pastel Mobile UI - Design System Profile
meta.purpose: Give an AI coding assistant (Cursor) enough context to generate new mobile screens and components in this exact visual language.
meta.source: Three iOS-style mobile screen mockups, reference viewport 393px wide.
meta.units: px (equal to pt) at a 393px-wide viewport. Scale proportionally for other widths.
meta.confidence: Colors marked 'exact' were shown as labelled swatches. All other values are visual estimates (about +/-10%). Preserve ratios and relationships over absolute numbers.
meta.content_policy: No source copy, brand names, or data are included. Use {placeholders} and generate realistic content for the new product.
meta.how_to_use: Save as .cursor/rules/design-system.json (or reference with @design-system.json). Ask Cursor to follow it strictly: tokens first, then layout archetypes, then components, then ai_generation_rules.

design_style.name: Soft Pastel Fintech
design_style.summary: Flat, airy, color-coded mobile UI. Large saturated-pastel surfaces carry meaning, very large tightly-tracked numerals and headlines create hierarchy, and a single near-black accent handles all primary actions.
principles: Color is information: each item or category gets one pastel surface; the whole screen can take on that pastel when focused on a single item.
Hierarchy comes from size and weight of type, not from borders, shadows or decoration.
One giant element per screen (headline, key number, or gauge) anchors the composition.
Tiny uppercase labels sit above values to give a clear label-over-value rhythm.
Text is always near-black ink on pastel. Never use white text on pastel surfaces.
Only one dark filled button per screen; everything secondary is outlined or a soft tinted chip.
Generous radii everywhere. Nothing has sharp corners.
Surfaces are flat. Depth is created by stacking (sheet over color field, card over card) not by shadows.
avoid: Drop shadows on cards or buttons
Saturated or neon colors; pure black backgrounds
Thin, low-contrast grey text on pastel backgrounds
More than one accent color per screen besides pastel category fills
Dense tables, hairline dividers between list items, sharp corners
Heavy bold weights for headlines (keep display type regular to medium)

color.notes: Three pastels are the identity. Any new category color must match their lightness and saturation range.

lavender.role: category fill / highlight tile / screen background

pastel_generation_rule.description: To add more category colors, keep HSL lightness 86-91% and saturation 70-97%, then vary hue only.

ink-900.role: primary text on pastel, primary button fill, gauge fill, dark chip fill

pine.role: alternative dark CTA/selected-chip fill when the screen is tinted blue-green. Same role as ink-900.

white.role: app background, bottom sheets, floating pill buttons

page-bg.role: canvas behind the app when shown in a presentation frame

sky-50.role: lighter inner card on a sky screen (tint of the screen color, about 40-50% lighter)

semantic_mapping.background.focus_screen: one pastel, full-bleed behind status bar
semantic_mapping.surface.sheet: white, radius-xl on top corners, overlaps the pastel field
semantic_mapping.text.caption: ink-400
semantic_mapping.action.tertiary: chip-on-pastel overlay or white floating pill

usage_rules: A screen is either white with pastel cards, or a full-bleed pastel with a white sheet or lighter inset card.
Never place two different pastels directly next to each other inside the same component, except a single highlight tile within a neutral row.
Soft chips on colored screens are made with the translucent dark overlay, never a new hue.
Ink on pastel must stay at contrast 7:1 or higher, which ink-900 does on all three pastels.

family.character: Modern neo-grotesque with slightly condensed, tight spacing. Clean numerals. No serif or mono in the UI.
family.features: font-feature-settings: 'tnum' on for prices, balances and any changing numbers.

display-hero.use: Single screen headline, left aligned, wraps onto 2-3 lines

display-amount.use: Key number on a focus screen

title-lg.use: Title inside an inset card or detail view

value-lg.use: Price/amount at bottom-right of a card

body-md.use: Card entity name, region name, key values

body-sm.use: Descriptive paragraph, pinned to the bottom of a card

label-micro.use: Label above a value, section labels, captions, tile dates

button-label.use: Primary and outlined button text, filter chips

typography.ratios: Display is about 4x body. Labels are much smaller than values. That extreme contrast between huge and tiny is the signature of the style.
rules: Display and value type is regular to medium weight with negative tracking. Never bold or black.
All-caps is reserved for micro labels, buttons and filter chips, always with positive tracking.
Left align everything except button labels and gauge center text.
Currency or unit symbols use the same size as the number; units after numbers (like a size unit or 'used') drop to caption size and ink-400.
Keep line-height under 1.05 for anything above 28px.

spacing.notes: Vertical rhythm is loose. Space between the header row and the hero headline is large (about 24-32), and space between the headline and the first card is about 24.

usage.device_frame: about 48 (mockup only, not part of the UI)

elevation.policy: Flat. No shadows on cards, sheets, or buttons.
exceptions: Floating white pill button on a white background may use a 1px outline of rgba(13,13,38,0.08) instead of a shadow.
Presentation frames around mockups may use a very soft, large-blur shadow, but this is not part of the app UI.
elevation.depth_technique: Stack layers: a white sheet overlaps the bottom of a pastel field, and an inset lighter card sits inside a slightly darker field, letting the edges of the underlying layer peek out at the sides.

borders.outlined_button: 1px solid ink-900 (on pastel) or 1px solid rgba(13,13,38,0.08) (on white)
borders.dividers: none. Use spacing instead of lines.
borders.selected_state: Filled with ink-900 (or pine) and white text, never a colored border

iconography.style: Simple, thin-to-regular outline glyphs (1.5px stroke, rounded caps), very small, monochrome ink.
patterns: Small circular badge (about 20-24px) with a simple mark next to an entity name, on a translucent white or dark circle.
Leading tiny chevron or x inside back/cancel pills.
Trailing plus icon in add pill.
Circle-outlined icon button (about 32-36px) for search or utility actions.
Cluster of 2-3 small rounded-square glyph badges (about 28px) that slightly overlap, used as a decorative meta row above a title.
iconography.rules: Icons never carry color. They inherit ink. No filled multicolor illustrations in the UI chrome.

layout.grid: Single column, full-width components, 20px side margins, no multi-column grids except a 3-column stats row.

device_chrome.status_bar: Time at left, system icons at right, over the screen's background color. Height about 54 including the notch area.
device_chrome.home_indicator: Short dark bar centered at the bottom, about 134x5 with full radius, 8px from the bottom edge.

structure: Header row: circular avatar left, white outlined pill button (label + plus icon) right
Vertical stack of full-width pastel cards, gap 8
Each card: top row = [badge + entity name] left, [region or type] right; bottom row = [primary detail in body-md + micro caption beneath] left, [value-lg] right
Card content is pinned to top and bottom edges (space-between) with a tall min-height of about 150-165
A_hero_and_stacked_cards.color_logic: Each card uses a different pastel. Cycle lavender, sky, blush (then extensions).

B_focus_screen_with_sheet.background: full-bleed pastel behind the status bar
structure: Title row: badge + entity name on the left, outlined small pill button on the right
Micro label, then display-amount directly below it
White bottom sheet rising from about 40% down the screen, radius-xl on top corners, runs to the bottom edge

Inside sheet: centered gauge, then 3-column stat row, then micro section label, then horizontally scrolling tile row (clipped at the right edge to imply scroll), then full-width primary button pinned near the bottom
Filter row: 3 pill chips (first selected = dark fill + white text, others outlined) + circular outlined icon button at the right end
Large inset card in a lighter tint of the pastel, margin 16, radius-lg, with the darker field visible around and slightly behind it

Inside the card, top to bottom: overlapping glyph badge cluster, title-lg, two label-over-value pairs, then flexible empty space, then body-sm paragraph, then full-width dark primary button at the very bottom

list_card.top_row: badge (20-24) + entity name (body-md) left; region/type (body-md) right, both ink-900
list_card.bottom_row: left: body-md primary detail with label-micro caption below; right: value-lg

states.focused: navigates to archetype B using the same pastel as the full-bleed background

primary_button.rule: One per screen, pinned near the bottom of its container.

outlined_small_button.use: Secondary action in a title row

filter_chip_group.selected: fill ink-900 (or pine), white button-label text

tile_row.layout: horizontal scroll, no scrollbar, gap 8, last tile clipped by the screen edge

tile.fill_highlight: a pastel (only the first / most recent tile)
tile.content: label-micro on top, value-sm at the bottom

inset_card.fill: sky-50 (lighter tint of the screen pastel)
inset_card.layout: flex column, title group at top, description and button pinned to bottom
inset_card.surrounding_field: screen pastel, visible as a border-like margin and slightly darker at the edges for a layered feel

glyph_badge_cluster.use: Decorative meta row above a title

bottom_sheet.overlap: rises over the pastel field, extends to the bottom edge including the safe area

gauge.track: 6-8 separated segments in gray-100 with 3-4px gaps between them
gauge.fill: solid ink-900 covering the first N segments, continuous stroke about 18-20px thick
gauge.caps: rounded start cap on the fill, small knob or tick at the start
gauge.center: value-gauge centered, caption below it in label-micro or 11px ink-400
gauge.implementation_hint: Use SVG stroke-dasharray or a set of arc paths; animate the fill with stroke-dashoffset over 600ms ease-out on mount.

data_visualization.style: Minimal. Big number plus one simple radial meter. No axes, gridlines, legends, or chart borders.
data_visualization.colors: Fill uses ink-900. Track uses gray-100. Highlights may use a single pastel.
data_visualization.labels: Micro uppercase labels for units and captions, big medium-weight numerals for the value.

motion.note: Not visible in static screens. These are inferred defaults that fit the style.
patterns: Tapping a card expands its pastel to fill the screen (shared-element transition), and the white sheet slides up from the bottom.
Selected filter chip fill cross-fades between chips.
Gauge fill animates from zero on entry.

accessibility.note: Chips visually 28-32px tall must have an invisible hit area of at least 44px.
accessibility.contrast: ink-900 on all pastels exceeds 7:1. ink-500 and ink-400 must only be used on white or on the lightest surfaces and only for non-essential captions.
accessibility.dynamic_type: Allow display sizes to scale down first when text grows. Never truncate values.
accessibility.color_alone: Pastel color-coding must be paired with a text label for the category.

must: Use only the tokens defined in this file. Do not invent new colors, radii, or font sizes.
Start every screen by choosing an archetype (A, B, or C) and follow its structure order exactly.
Assign one pastel per item or category and use ink-900 text on it.
Put exactly one dark filled primary button per screen, at the bottom of its container.
Make one element huge (hero headline, key number, or gauge) and keep everything else small.
Pair every value with a tiny uppercase micro label placed above or below it.
Keep surfaces flat: no shadows, gradients, or dividers.
Use tabular numerals for all numbers and negative letter-spacing for large type.
Use radius tokens consistently: 20 for cards, 16 for buttons, 28 for sheet tops, pill for chips.
Generate realistic placeholder content appropriate to the new product. Never reuse content from the source screens.
must_not: Add shadows, gradients, glass effects, or borders on cards
Use white text on pastel surfaces
Use more than one dark button per screen
Use bold or black font weights for display type
Add more than one non-pastel accent hue
Use hairline separators between list items
ai_generation_rules.adapting_to_new_domains: Swap the content model, keep the visual model. A card is always: [badge + name] top-left, [type] top-right, [detail + caption] bottom-left, [big value] bottom-right. A focus screen is always: pastel field, key number, white sheet with meter, stats, tiles and a primary button.
self_check_before_output: Does the screen have exactly one dominant element?
Are all colors from the token list?
Is every surface flat with correct radii?
Is there exactly one primary button?
Are micro labels uppercase with positive tracking and large type tightly tracked?
Is text ink-900 on every pastel?
ai_generation_rules.prompt_template: Build a {screen_name} for {product_description} following design-system.json. Use archetype {A|B|C}. Use {framework: React + Tailwind | SwiftUI | Flutter | React Native}. Map tokens from css_variables or tailwind_theme_extend. Generate realistic placeholder data and do not copy any text from the reference. Mobile-first at 393px width.
